## Build transparent evidence maps from scientific literature

This full-day workshop teaches a deterministic, non-generative LLM pipeline for systematic reviews. Participants move from bulk paper retrieval to causal relation extraction, then build a nomological knowledge graph from published claims.

## Why this workshop

- Deterministic, evidence-based pipeline with no generative AI.
- End-to-end workflow from APIs and PDFs to extractable sentence datasets.
- Structured causal extraction using `rasoultilburg/SocioCausaNet`.
- Reproducible outputs suitable for theory-building and systematic reviews.

## Learning outcomes

By the end of the workshop, participants will be able to:

- Retrieve papers in bulk via public APIs (Semantic Scholar, PubMed, CrossRef).
- Convert PDFs to clean text and handle common extraction artifacts.
- Prepare sentence-level corpora using light NLP preprocessing.
- Apply transformer tooling for deterministic sentence analysis.
- Extract and harmonize causal claims into a nomological map.

## Curriculum at a glance

| Module | Focus | Output |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Bulk Paper Retrieval via API | API keys, search features, bulk download | Local paper corpus + metadata |
| 2. PDF to Text Conversion | Tool comparison, extraction, cleaning | Plain-text corpus |
| 3. Sentence Extraction & Preprocessing | Segmentation and artifact handling | Sentence dataset for model inference |
| 4. Introduction to HuggingFace | Model cards, sentence vs token tasks, pipeline API | Runnable inference notebook |
| 5. Causal Extraction & Knowledge Graph | SocioCausaNet inference, harmonization, graph build | Queryable nomological map |
